notYet: Not yet part of Africa and the Indian Ocean

stages.name: Unknown or legendary coasts
stages.desc: Beyond what sailors reliably knew: rumour, legend or half-lost reports

stages.name: Coasts known from voyages
stages.desc: Coasts reached and described by recorded voyages and traders

stages.name: India trade route
stages.desc: Ports and lands on the sea route from Egypt to India

stages.name: Ptolemaic Egypt
stages.desc: The Greek kingdom of the Ptolemies, ruled from Alexandria

stages.name: Mauretanian kingdom
stages.desc: The kingdom of the Mauri, west of Numidia, ruled by its own kings

stages.name: Gades and Roman Spain
stages.desc: Phoenician Gades, allied to Rome, and the Roman provinces of Hispania

states.name: India
timeline: Known to Greeks since Alexander; Nearchus' fleet sailed its north-west coast in 325 BC
Eudoxus reaches India and brings back perfumes and precious stones
A Greek envoy, Heliodorus, raises a pillar to Vasudeva at Vidisha (about this year)

states.name: Somalia
timeline: South of the Cape of Spices, a coast unknown to Greek sailors
Blown south, Eudoxus lands here, records local words and finds the horse-head prow

states.name: Somaliland
timeline: Greek traders buy myrrh and frankincense along this coast as far as the Cape of Spices

states.name: Morocco
timeline: The Mauretanian kingdom; Gades' small 'horse' boats fish its coast as far as the Lixus river
Eudoxus urges King Bogus to back the voyage, then flees a plot to maroon him (date approximate)
King Bocchus I joins his son-in-law Jugurtha against Rome
Bocchus hands Jugurtha to Sulla and becomes Rome's ally

states.name: W. Sahara
timeline: Desert coast beyond the Lixus, known only from old, half-lost reports such as Hanno's
Eudoxus' first Atlantic voyage probably follows this coast south before turning back

states.name: Oman
timeline: Frankincense coast of southern Arabia, known through Arab traders

states.name: Spain
timeline: Roman Hispania; Gades, founded by Phoenicians from Tyre, is a free city allied to Rome
Eudoxus reaches Gades, builds a great ship and two tow-boats (date approximate)
Eudoxus sails from Iberia a last time with seed, tools and carpenters (date approximate)

states.name: Sudan
timeline: Red Sea coast of the 'Troglodytes', where Ptolemaic hunters once caught war elephants

states.name: Djibouti
timeline: The strait at the mouth of the Red Sea, where the open ocean begins
Gateway of the new direct sea route to India

states.name: Eritrea
timeline: Red Sea coast sailed by Ptolemaic hunters and traders

states.name: Senegal
timeline: Perhaps reached by Hanno of Carthage centuries earlier; no one in Gades could say

states.name: Egypt
timeline: Ptolemy VIII Euergetes II and Cleopatra III rule from Alexandria
Euergetes dies; Cleopatra III reigns with her son Ptolemy IX
Cleopatra drives out Ptolemy IX and reigns with his brother, Ptolemy X Alexander

states.name: Yemen
timeline: Saba and the ports of Arabia Felix sell Indian goods on to Egypt
Greek ships now sail past Arabia straight across the ocean to India
Traditional starting year of the Himyarite era, the calendar of a rising south Arabian power

states.name: Mauritania
timeline: Unknown to Mediterranean sailors
Eudoxus' last voyage heads down this coast; he is never heard of again

states.name: Gambia
timeline: Unknown to Mediterranean sailors

events.title: Envoy from Cyzicus
events.text: Eudoxus of Cyzicus comes to Alexandria as a sacred envoy announcing his city's games, and stays at the court of Ptolemy VIII.

events.title: A castaway Indian
events.text: Coast guards on the Red Sea find a half-dead Indian sailor on a stranded ship and bring him to the king.

events.title: Sailing for India
events.text: With the Indian as pilot and gifts from the king, Eudoxus sails down the Red Sea from Egypt's ports.

events.title: Bab el-Mandeb
events.text: The ship leaves the Red Sea through the narrow strait into the open ocean.

events.title: The monsoon crossing
events.text: The summer monsoon from the south-west carries the ship across the Arabian Sea.

events.title: Landfall in India
events.text: Eudoxus trades the king's gifts for perfumes and precious stones, perhaps at a west-coast port like Barygaza.

events.title: Arabia Felix bypassed
events.text: Aden and the Arabian ports had long passed Indian goods on to Egypt; now Greek ships sail straight past.

events.title: The winter monsoon
events.text: The north-east monsoon of winter brings the ship back toward the Red Sea.

events.title: Cargo confiscated
events.text: Back in Alexandria, Ptolemy VIII takes the whole cargo for himself.

events.title: Death of Euergetes
events.text: Ptolemy VIII dies in June after more than fifty years as king; Cleopatra III reigns with her son Ptolemy IX.

events.title: The second voyage
events.text: Cleopatra sends Eudoxus back to India with a larger outfit.

events.title: Blown off course
events.text: On the way home, winds drive Eudoxus south, past the Horn of Africa.

events.title: Bread, wine and figs
events.text: Landing on an unknown coast, he wins friends with gifts, takes on water and pilots, and writes down local words.

events.title: The horse-head prow
events.text: On this coast he finds the wooden prow of a wrecked ship carved with a horse, and takes it with him.

events.title: Stripped again
events.text: In Egypt, now ruled by Cleopatra's son, he is accused of embezzlement and loses everything.

events.title: Pilots identify the prow
events.text: In the harbour market, shipmasters say the prow comes from the fishing boats of Gades.

events.title: Himyarite era
events.text: The Himyarite calendar of south Arabia counts its years from about this time.

events.title: Temple of Melqart
events.text: Near Gades stands the great temple of Melqart, the Phoenician god the Greeks called Heracles.

events.title: The 'horse' boats
events.text: Poor fishermen of Gades sail small boats with horse-head prows down the African coast as far as the Lixus.

events.title: Mogador
events.text: An island off Morocco's Atlantic coast, once the farthest Phoenician trading post known on this coast.

events.title: Homeward to Cyzicus
events.text: Convinced Africa can be sailed around, Eudoxus goes home and puts all his property on board.

events.title: Dicaearchia
events.text: He calls at Dicaearchia, Rome's busiest port, announcing his plan and trading for funds.

events.title: Massalia
events.text: He sails on to the Greek city of Massalia and along the coast toward Spain.

events.title: Heliodorus pillar
events.text: In India, Heliodorus, envoy of a Greek king of the north-west, raises a stone pillar at Vidisha.

events.title: Fitting out at Gades
events.text: At Gades he builds a great ship and two tow-boats, and takes on musicians, doctors and craftsmen.

events.title: Through the Pillars
events.text: Eudoxus sails out past the Pillars of Heracles and turns south, with westerly winds behind him.

events.title: Massacre at Cirta
events.text: Jugurtha of Numidia takes Cirta and kills the Italian merchants there; Rome goes to war.

events.title: Run aground
events.text: The tired crew hugs the shore and the great ship grounds; from its timbers they build a fifty-oared boat.

events.title: Familiar words
events.text: Farther south he meets people whose words match those he wrote down in East Africa, and turns back.

events.title: The wooded island
events.text: On the way back he notes an uninhabited island with water and trees, perhaps one of the Canaries.

events.title: The court of Bogus
events.text: In Mauretania he urges King Bogus to back the voyage; the king's friends warn it would open the kingdom to invaders.

events.title: Flight from Mauretania
events.text: Learning he is to be marooned on a desert island, he flees to Roman territory and crosses to Spain.

events.title: The last departure
events.text: With a round ship, a fifty-oared boat, seed, farm tools and carpenters, he sails to winter on his island and go on.

events.title: Vanished
events.text: Here Posidonius' trail ends: what happened next, he writes, the people of Gades and Iberia may know.

events.title: Metellus in Numidia
events.text: The consul Metellus takes command against Jugurtha and fights him at the river Muthul.

events.title: Marius takes command
events.text: Gaius Marius, consul for the first time, takes over the war in Africa.

events.title: Ptolemy IX ousted
events.text: Cleopatra III drives Ptolemy IX out of Alexandria and makes his brother Ptolemy X her co-ruler.

events.title: Bocchus defeated
events.text: Marius defeats Jugurtha and his ally Bocchus of Mauretania near Cirta.

events.title: Jugurtha betrayed
events.text: Bocchus I hands Jugurtha over to the young Sulla, ending the war and binding Mauretania to Rome.

chartNote: Share of the area of the fifteen present-day countries on this map, by what each was to Greek and Roman sailors of the time. Regions are today's boundaries, a simplification: a coast could be known while its interior was not. The story rests on one source, Posidonius as quoted by Strabo, and the dates after 116 BC are approximate.
